title: Transportation
description: Thailand has many transportation options, from trains and buses to taxis and ride-hailing apps.
tips: Use BTS and MRT in Bangkok to avoid traffic.
Grab and other ride-hailing services are convenient in many cities.
Always check the fare before taking a taxi or negotiate the price for some local services.
For long-distance travel, trains, buses, and domestic flights are common options.

title: SIM Card & Internet
description: Staying connected is easy with tourist SIM cards and eSIM options available at airports and stores.
tips: Tourist SIM cards are available at major airports.
Check whether your phone is unlocked before using a local SIM.
eSIM can be a convenient option if your phone supports it.
Keep your passport ready when purchasing a SIM card.

title: Weather
description: Thailand is generally warm throughout the year, but weather conditions vary by region and season.
tips: Wear lightweight and breathable clothing.
Carry an umbrella during the rainy season.
Use sunscreen and drink plenty of water.
Check the local weather forecast before outdoor activities.

title: Emergency Numbers
description: Keep important emergency numbers available while traveling in Thailand.
tips: Tourist Police: 1155
Police: 191
Medical Emergency: 1669
Fire and Rescue: 199

title: Thai Culture & Etiquette
description: Understanding basic Thai etiquette can make your trip more comfortable and respectful.
tips: A polite smile and respectful attitude are appreciated.
Remove your shoes before entering some homes and religious places.
Avoid touching someone's head.
Be respectful when visiting temples and religious sites.

title: Dress Code
description: Dress comfortably for the weather while respecting local customs.
tips: Wear modest clothing when visiting temples.
Cover shoulders and knees in many religious sites.
Lightweight clothing is suitable for hot weather.
Bring a light jacket for air-conditioned places.

title: Food & Dining
description: Thailand is famous for its diverse and flavorful food culture.
tips: Try popular dishes such as Pad Thai, Tom Yum, and Mango Sticky Rice.
Tell restaurant staff about food allergies before ordering.
Street food can be a great way to experience local cuisine.
If you have dietary restrictions, ask about ingredients before eating.

title: Money & Payments
description: Thai Baht (THB) is the official currency of Thailand.
tips: Keep some cash for local markets and small shops.
Credit cards are commonly accepted in hotels and larger businesses.
ATMs are widely available in cities and tourist areas.
Check exchange rates before converting your money.
